newsitem.title: SPAIN: Motor racing-Mansell makes slow start to comeback.
newsitem.headline: Motor racing-Mansell makes slow start to comeback.

text.p: Nigel Mansell, minus his famous moustache, made a slow comeback to Formula One motor racing on Wednesday as he began two days of testing with the Jordan team at the Circuit de Catalunya.

The 1992 world champion, looking fit and relaxed, was the slowest driver of the 10 taking part in the winter session in the cold mists of the Catalan hinterland behind Barcelona, clocking a best time of one minute and 23.34 seconds during the morning.

This left him about seven-tenths of a second down on the best efforts of his temporary -- and possibly future -- team-mate Ralf Schumacher of Germany, the 21-year-old younger son of double world champion Michael Schumacher, but nearly four seconds behind the pace-setting lap of Canadian Jacques Villeneuve in a Williams.
Villeneuve, who finished runner-up in the 1996 drivers' championship, set the pace ahead of Austrian Gerhard Berger in a Benetton and Briton David Coulthard in a McLaren.

The 43-year-old Mansell, watched by a few spectators scattered around the empty grandstands, acknowledged the presence of the small international media corps gathered to see if he could reproduce his old pace and elan, but opted not to speak during the lunch-break.
The gentle easing-in process suggested he was taking his time to find his Formula One feet again after more than 18 months out of the cockpit.

"It's a bit of a gamble for us, but if you want to win in Formula One you have to take risks," said a Jordan spokesman. "Nigel is a risk, of course, but if he is fast and motivated then it will be a risk worth taking for us all."
